utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case number IT-05-88-T, The Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I know, I know, I saw it but if you want -- I don't know how you're going to do it because I am technically minded but not to this extent. And I will be with Judge Orie later on in any case, so it doesn't matter. For the record -- shall I continue or not? The thing is on one side it's okay, it's on the other side that it isn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sorry if I am am bothering you with this, but at least what I tried did work and we have eliminated Judge Orie's courtroom. I would like some advice from you Madam Registrar, if we could proceed? If it has worked with me it should work with others. But -- and I can tell you what I did. I logged off completely, logged on again, I didn't switch off, I logged off only from -- I didn't actually log off, I just closed the internet connection. Closed the internet connection and re-opened it again. All right. Connecting then with the central distributing section. So, Madam Registrar, has called the case. For the record all the accused are present today. Mr. Nikolic, Mr. Nikolic, yesterday, I did see your client's waiver in relation to yesterday's sitting but we still haven't got it from the horse's mouth that he waived his right to be present for the sitting when he felt sick and was taken to the Detention Unit of two days ago. So Mr. Beara, it was two days ago that we were informed that you were not feeling well and we sent you you back to the Detention Unit. At the time we had an indication that a waiver was forthcoming, a formal waiver was forthcoming for you, but we received the waiver for the day after and for yesterday, we never received a proper waiver for that part of the sitting. I would like you to confirm here in open court that you had waived your rights to be present while we continue. THE ACCUSED BEARA: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, present today more or less it's the same composition of yesterday. I just notice the absence of Mr. Krgovic and Mr. Ostojic. And good morning, General Pandurevic, and good morning to you, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Sorry for the delay but these things happen. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And thank you for the technical advice. It worked for me too.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And before I continue with the examination of Mr. Pandurevic, there's something I want to say. This is a public court which is widely broadcast and reported and it brings upon advocates an extra duty of responsibility in their advocacy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Make-up assistance or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: General Gvero is a serious and dignified man and his legal team are highly professional, hard working, and I respect them very much and I should not have made a joke in my opening statement at their expense. And I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Everyone took it in its own strength. But let's continue. But I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Could I say, so do we and I am sure may client does as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We left off yesterday Mr. Pandurevic, on the 11th of July, and I just want to backtrack a little bit simply to address a couple of documents. And the first of them is 7D761.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So I would be obliged if that could be placed into e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And this is a Drina Corps interim combat report from the 6th of July, and it records the fact that the enemy offered very strong resistance particularly on the Zelini Jadar-Srebrenica axis where the was significantly weaker on the village - of I can't read that - they fortified their defensive positions well, especially on the approaches to Srebrenica. What sort of input did you have in to the writing of a report like that which was written, we see, by General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This type of report are written based on the information received in the course of combat operations. General Krstic had an opportunity to personally observe the progress of the fighting, and he also received reports from subordinate commanders and units participating in the operation. Therefore, this is an aggregate compilation of the information received from the units and on a personal basis. So this report contains information about my tactical group that was involved in combat operations on that day along the Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And can we now have a look, please, at 7D762.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is a combat report, an interim combat report from the 9th of July. Have you had an opportunity to read it through? And what events does this record and reflect?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a report relating to the 9th of July, 1995. It provides small details about the situation and it covers a larger number of features where combat operations were carried out. It includes the features captured by the combat group of Birac Brigade and other brigades as well as some important features captured by my contact tactical group. We can also see that there is a decision taken by the commander of the operation relating to further operations. I cannot see from this document at what time this report was drafted and sent out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, it's not material for my purposes. I'd prefer to go on, please, to 7D474, the interim combat report from the 10th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And we see in the first paragraph, it says at 0430: "The enemy carried out a powerful counter-attack along the Srebrenica-Bojna-Zeleni Jadar village axis. They took control of the Zivko Brdo feature. Throughout the day the enemy put up fierce resistance to our forces using all weapons at their disposal. Our forces halted the enemy counter- attack and at about 1300 hours regained control of the Zivkovo Brdo --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I thought I was going slowly enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: "By 2000 hours they reached the Divljakinje-Banja-Crni-Guber-Bojna, a big bend at the entrance to Srebrenica. Elevation 372, Vagan, Alibegovac-Selo-Bucje line, paving the way to entering Srebrenica. Our losses: Six soldiers killed and 10 wounded." Does that accurately record the events in combat on the 10th of July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report, particularly item 2, reflects the situation on the grounds, as I described yesterday. The number of the wounded and the killed refers mainly to members of the tactical group 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll come back now to where we left off yesterday. After you had met with General Krstic in the morning, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the morning of the 11th near the repeater on the Bojna feature, I received an order from General Krstic to proceed with my units with further actions to try to take control of the town and the surrounding features which were important for taking and maintaining control of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were they important features to the south of the town or, as it were, around the town?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is common knowledge that Srebrenica is a town which a completely surrounded by what soldiers call strong topographic features which are convenient for defence. At one point, I thought that the 28th Division was putting up weak resistance on the afternoon of the 10th and the morning of the 11th. Therefore, their aim was to try and pull in our forces into the ground and -- into the town, and then launch an attack on our forces from the surrounding features. For that purpose, I deemed these features to be very important to our control before entering the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where were those features?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These features were around the town itself, literally above the streets you have slopes and on my axis of attack, there was a feature north-east towards Banja-Crni-Guber, and on the left-hand side west of the town was a smaller feature covered with pinewood. And more to the west, the general area was to be covered by the 2nd Romanija and 1st Birac Brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you take those features and if so by what time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did. East of the town combat group 2 and the company's from the battalion took control of the features closest to the town, and elements of the Podrinje detachment went into the town and some elements took control of a feature which was west of town literally above the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what time the day did that all occur?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all occurred, as far as I can remember, after 1500 hours. Let's say 1600 hours or possibly 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And where were you yourself while this was going on?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was moving along the main road leading directly to the town of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Who were you with?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My driver, my signalman, and my escort were with me, and also Dragutinovic, the operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you get into the town?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said. I cannot be exactly sure about the time, but it was definitely in the afternoon, after 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I want to refresh your memory by showing you a section of the trial video. It's P2047. CD 6. And the section I want you to look at is about 3 minutes long. It's between 2800 hours and 3112. I'm sorry, 28 minutes and 31 minutes and 12 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] Go forward, you can salute me when we get to Bratunac from here. Look in that shelter down there. Search it quickly. Trivic, is that you? "It's my General, sir, and I thought it was some fucking -- "Let's exchange. "Well done. "Two years ago you we took the flat to Trnovo, two years ago today at this time, two years ago on July 11th, congratulations. "Congratulations, General this is free. And we finally meet, hello commander. Major Ljubo, sir, Mr. President. And you must be Ljubo, Ljubo Markan. Four times so far. Good. Excellent. Let's go boys, Trivic, Trivic don't, forget history, please. Move forward so we can get to Bratunac, come on forget history. Move on. "I've been ordered to occupy this position General, sir. "Move on to Bratunac please, the centre should go forward. Leave the centre be. Move forward with your men. Tell them I'm here. I want them to advance to Bratunac. Let's go. Move chief, so I don't have to bother with you. Go, go, go. "This one is for the command. The ammunition is on the truck. Where is the truck? It's right here here. Whose ammunition is it? It's for Legenda. Requisition it. Run the truck and go forward. Go, go forward, come on move. "What is this? "Commander, sir, it's all right. It's all right. "Trivic. "Yes? "Payments for services in German marks only. Change only. There is a man up there peering out from the second floor. "Run. Take advantage of the panic among the Turks. What are these troops doing here? What are you doing here? I hope to God we do this soon in down-town Gorazde. God willing, come on. Up there, up there on the top. Faster, faster, get in. "What? Are they waiting for you? Come on, quickly, take it and move on towards Bratunac. Right away. There is shooting up there. Here we are on July 11th, 1995, in Serb Srebrenica. On the eve of yet another great Serb holiday, we give this town to the Serbian people as a gift. Finally, after the rebellion against the Dahis, the time has come to take revenge on the Turks in this region. Those hills and the part of the Hoda [phoen]. We are going straight to Bratunac men, straight to Potocari. "First we have to take the hills, General. "Do whatever you have to do. You shouldn't get out. "If you please, is this where, this is the main high-rise buildings that are there. "Yes, they are 300 to 400 metres. "Congratulations, chief. Good luck. Straight to Bratunac, go on guys. Troops go straight to Bratunac."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do we have the coordinates of this recording, where it started.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It started at 28 minutes and it ended at 31.21, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Firstly, to your recollection about what time of the day was all that glad handing and kissing going on?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was going on after I entered the town with my troops. And east and west of the town on the elevated points. I suppose that this could have been around 1600 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you kiss General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What was your mood at the time we saw you in that video?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in a good mood. There was no special reason for me to be in a particular good mood for various reasons. First of all, on the previous day we were engaged in heavy fighting. We were forced to retake what we had already occupied once in fighting and for a soldier, that is the most difficult task of all. Second of all, I'd suffered losses in my unit. Five or six fallen soldiers and some dozen wounded, several were still counted as missing. I knew that the complete 28th Division was in that area. However, we had lost contact with it and that's the worst thing in fighting, when you lose contact with the retreating enemy. And actually, you have to start chasing the enemy on its back. And that's how we created another new problem, which is that the 28th Division had disappeared from the area and we had lost contact with it. Second of all, I saw those men that turned up on the streets of the town whose axes of attack were not the town at all. Their units had remained to the east or to the west, and they had descended into town to meet with Mladic. And as I saw it in Mr. Trivic's journal who noted that he was not able to sell his success, under inverted commas, but obviously this was an attempt to do something of this sort in Srebrenica. On the 11th in the morning, I also saw the members of the 10th sabotage unit who had turned up at the moment when the 28th Division no longer presented danger because their resistance had been broken, and I really didn't understand why these troops would appear in the area, for what reason. And finally, I'd say last but not least, I was tired. I was exhausted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What did you think people should be focusing their attention on at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our main task was to fight and engage with the 28th Division. That should have been our main objective, our main concern, our main task.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, we saw a number of people on that video. Obviously Mr. Trivic has been here and identified himself. There was another man referred to by his first name which was Ljubo. Who was that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ljubo Eric, major. He was in command of the 2nd combat group from the Romanija motorised brigade, or rather 2nd Romanija Mechanised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Trivic, did he have any command function in relation to Krivaja 95?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Colonel Trivic was the part of the 2nd Romania Mechanised Brigade. As far as I can remember he was present during the commander's reconnaissance on the 1st of July, and he took a combat group a -- tantamount to a reinforced company. They were supposed to participate in Krivaja 95 operation. He appointed a commander of that combat group, Major Ljubo Eric, and he established a command. As far as I understand his role, he was supposed to assist Ljubo Eric in certain situations. However, up until the 11th of July until the moment he met up with Mladic and until the moment Mladic issued Colonel Andric, the commander of the Birac Brigade, Trivic, and other brigade commanders to be personally engaged in combat, he didn't do anything. So as from that moment on, he had somewhat broader autonomy. He could stay in the territory, but he could also leave it which means that his position and my position were not absolutely identical. It would have been too much for a brigade commander to be put in command of a company.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You've mentioned Colonel Andric. Did we see him on the video?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw him on the video. I did not see him during combat. I did not hear him on the radio. The combat group from his brigade was commanded by Major Nemanja Pavlovic. According to Andric's statements he appeared on the area on the 9th or in the 10th, he came to inspect the unit, and then he remained in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was there anybody else we saw in that section of the video, who in your recollection, had nothing to do with the combat operation?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw Lieutenant-Colonel Radomir Furtula, the commander of the 5th Podrinje Brigade. In Krivaja 95 operation, he did not have any of his forces. He was not engaged. Why he turned up there, where from, I'm not clear to this very day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, what was it that you were suggesting to General Mladic should be done in the short section of video where we saw you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had noticed that group of officers, Mladic, Krstic, Zivanovic, and others that have been mentioned. I saw them moving through Srebrenica in a rather theatrical way, without being aware of the situation ahead of them. And I believed judging by the measures of combat security that we were supposed to use our own forces to secure the area first, and then let the commanders proceed in advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What did you do after you spoke to General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He told me do as you please. I acted upon my own will. I deployed my troops in keeping with the tactical situation, I took smaller forces and I continued moving through the town towards the centre, and I went all the way to the football pitch in Gostilj village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you see any inhabitants in the town?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I did not see any inhabitants in the town. Only in the UNPROFOR base, whether they called that bravo company. In the former textile factory, I saw several elderly people and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And where did you go after you had been in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was still in Srebrenica, I inspected my troops. I issued tasks for them, I looked at the police station as the place for my command, and then I was called by General Krstic to attend a meeting in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What time did you leave the town?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was summer and night falls somewhat later in the day and it was already dark. Not complete dark, so I believe that it may have been between 2130 and 2145 hours, around that period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you leave on foot or in a car?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took my car there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Who did you leave with?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My driver, my signalsman, and my escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And which route did you take?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Srebrenica-Potocari-Bratunac was the route.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: When you passed through Potocari, what did you see?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would rather call it trying to break through to the masses. At one moment, I regretted having opted for that route because there were huge numbers of people on the road and around it, and it was difficult to go through. However, since I'd already chosen that route, I didn't have a choice. I proceeded. I managed to break through the masses and finally I arrived in Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: At about what time?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been around 2200 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And when you got there, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went to the command of the Bratunac Brigade, because that was the venue of the meeting to which I'd been called.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where there other people there when you got there?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were people, yes. There were officers. I don't know whether I arrived before other commanders or they arrived before me, I'm not sure. I only know that there was quite a number of officers attending that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where was the meeting held?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting was held in a room in the command of the Bratunac Brigade. I don't know whether that was their ops room or a meeting room, I'm not sure. Because this would have been my second or third visit of that command, so I was really not very familiar with the layout of the building or where the rooms were in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And how long after you arrived did the meeting commence?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meeting started soon thereafter, as soon as I arrived we took our seats in that room and the meeting started.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: About how many people were present?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember very well that General Krstic was there. And I believe that at the very beginning of the meeting, General Mladic was not there, he joined us later. There were also the commanders of the brigades that had been in the area the previous day, and I'm not sure whether there was anybody else from the command of the Bratunac Brigade. I would say that there were about ten or so people present.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: How long did the meeting last?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A meeting of that sort was more of a monologue by one man and issuing task. It was not really a meeting that would deal with an analysis or an exchange of opinions. It did not last long. After the meeting we moved to an adjacent room where dinner had been prepared for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Who conducted the monologue?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As soon as he turned up for the meeting, General Mladic took the floor. He reviewed the events of the previous day. He issued an order for the units to be ready to proceed towards Zepa. He also said that we should make the most of that chaotic situation in the 28th Division and defeat them as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In the transcript it appears that you said, "he reviewed the events of the previous day." Is that what he did?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not of the previous day, but rather that same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did anybody else speak other than General Mladic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My proposal to General Mladic was to establish contact with the 28th Division as soon as possible, that we should learn where they were and what their intentions were, and that we should assign forces that would be engaged in a combat with that division. And that the rest of the forces should remain in Srebrenica and Bratunac in order to stabilize the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did anybody else speak?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as far as I can remember, nobody did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what response did you get to your suggestions?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The response was you heard the order, you heard what the tasks are, prepare units and proceed towards Zepa ASAP.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did everybody who had attended the meeting go to the adjacent room for a meal that you've told us about?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly who went for the meal. I know that I did. There were other men there, that did not last long, and immediately after that I returned to the police station in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What was the meal?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meal had been prepared by Zvanko Bajagic who was a member of the office of the Drina Corps, of the staff office there. And he had been known to prepare food for the corps command on similar occasions. He had brought fish, I think it was carp. I'm not a big aficionado of fish, but I did eat. And that was the last day of a fast, according to the orthodox calendar. It was St. Peter's day and it was the end of fasting and fish had to be served, it's a staple food during the time of fasting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Which route did you take back to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't take the same route if view of the situation that I had encountered on arrival. People from the Bratunac Brigade told me about another route leading via Sas, along the Sas lake, and a feature called Gradac, then you take a detour, a macadam road straight to Srebrenica, and this is the route that I took.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I just want to consider with you one document. It's P111.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is, I suppose, a report of a prisoner who had been captured on the 12th of July and interviewed. And if we look at the second paragraph it says: "Despite his limited intellectual capacity, he gave the following information during the interview on the situation in the Suceska area. He said that all military-aged men in the Suceska area have been organised and have set off under the command of Zulfo Tursunovic to cross the territory of Republika Srpska illegally to Kladanj and Tuzla." Given what you've told us you've said during the meeting in Bratunac that evening, was any information of that sort available to calm your fears?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th in the evening on that meeting, I could not receive detailed information about the location and the intentions of the 28th Division from anybody. Our assessments were based on the information that we obtained in the course of the day after the bombardment of our positions and the surveillance of the radio connections of the 28th Division. This is intelligence that was received from Mr. Beklesh [phoen] from Udinem [phoen] who had been taken prisoner of war. And this was taken on the 12th, which means that as of that day, our information about the intentions and the location of the 28th Division became much more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was anything said at that meeting that you attended about anybody knowing where the 28th Division were going?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nothing was said. Nobody provided us with any exact information about the whereabouts of the 28th Division. However, starting from the military logic, and we know that the officers of the 28th Division shared the same logic and abided by the same rules as we did in the VRS, and the rule was that a unit when encircled tries to break through in the direction of their closest unit and that that breakthrough should be carried out in several directions. That's why I assume that as elements of the 28th Division, most of them will try to breakthrough towards Kladanj, less towards Kalesija and Tuzla, and also one part of the elements will try to break through towards Zepa. That was how I assessed the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just one more question on that topic and then I'll move to something that you just hinted at. Was there any information at the meeting you attended to suggest any prisoners by then had been taken?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't have any such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you've hinted at the answer to the next question, which is knowing the terrain as you did, where did you think it was most likely the forces of the 28th Division would go?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought that the Srebrenica-Kladanj would be the shortest route. I knew that they used to use it before for providing supplies and moving units, and therefore, I assumed that the bulk of their forces might take this route again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And which territory of Republika Srpska would that take them across?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would pass practically through the zone of operations of the Drina Corps. Anyway, whichever route they decided to take, that would be through the area in the zone of the Drina Corps, and the area where a large number of Serbian settlements were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You've told us that you spent the night at the police station in Srebrenica. Where were your units on the night of the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units remained in the positions I mentioned earlier, and that is on the northern edge of the town, i.e., the village of Gostiljca [as interpreted] and the football pitch and on these mild slopes above the town itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And was that all of them, all three battle groups, or combat groups, so as I don't offends Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody who was under my command as member of the tactical group were in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Sorry, I'm just invited to correct another transcription of your evidence. The evening of the meeting, was that St. Peter's day, or was St. Peter's day the following day?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: St. Peter's day is on the 12th of July, so that would have been the next day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So let's come to the next day. What did you do on the morning of the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the morning of the 12th of July, I again inspected my positions. I spent most of the time in the village of Gostilj with elements of the Podrinje detachment and their commander, aka Legenda.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I want to leave you there for a moment, and show you a few exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I want to look at the Zvornik Brigade duty officer's notebook for the 12th of July. So that's P377. And we need to see page 114 both languages, please. And we are going to need to see the very bottom of the page. It's the last entry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: On my screen it's quite hard to read, Mr. Pandurevic. Can you read the handwritten document in Serbian? I'll read it to you slowly in English. The passage I'm interested in. It says: "Radika requested assistance in manpower to stop the Turks. We are sending Praga. Bring it from Brezanci, Mane, SUP to his men on the ground. Give him Radika's phone number." Do you know who Radika is or was?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain 1st Class Radika Petrovic was a commander of a battalion. It says here the 8th Infantry Battalion. That was how it was designated while it was part of the Zvornik Brigade but at the time it was the 4th Battalion of the Bratunac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what about Mane, do you know who that is or was?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe this is Mane Djuric, deputy chief of the public security centre in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have a look at P1103. It's D in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The document is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm very sorry. I should have known that. Can we then not -- we'll, actually we're going to have to go into private session because I'm going to have to ask some questions on the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's easier. Let's go into private session for a short while, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, everybody, very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pandurevic, you know what this document is. It's a transcript of an intercepted communication, and it begins: "Hello, General, I've spoken with Mane." It's recorded at being at 7.55 in the morning. "Good. One of our companies is up there with a bulldozer man there in Konjevic Polje. He has the task of doing whatever it does. So you may order through the commander what he is to do, and for your information, he has reserves. It's not necessary. "... that's it, I'm also sending this Praga, and I'm working on this with my police in the depth in the territory. They've probably informed you a large column of Turkish groups in pouring into Rainci. "In Rainci. "In Rainci, yes, that's across from Bule. "We are taking action in that area. We are both in touch with the situation. All right. Okay. I don't know if there's any artillery ammunition. I forwarded a request yesterday. I sent a lot up there, to my boss." Now, what army unit would you expect to be responsible for a bulldozer?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's mention here, a bulldozer unit in Konjevic Polje. I know that at the time there was the 5th Engineers Battalion of the Drina Corps in Konjevic Polje, and this is probably refers this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And while you were engaged with tactical group 1 in Zeleni Jadar, did you ever ask the brigade command in Zvornik to send you any ammunition?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that on the 5th of July when I arrived on the -- Pribicevac to inspect the tank company which had arrived there a day earlier, I inspected their combat readiness level and the level of preparedness and to my surprise they didn't have the entire ammunition kit for their tanks. For that reason through the forward command post of the corps, I established communication with Zvornik and requested ammunition to be sent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You've answered this question earlier, but in terms of geographical proximity, Brezanci and Konjevic Polje, how close are they together?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I'm not very familiar with that terrain, Brezanci are somewhere between Bratunac and Milici. It was in the area of responsibility of the battalion commanded by Radika Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, let's leave that document and that conversation to one side for a moment. Can you explain how the telephones in the commander's office, the Chief of Staff's office, and the duty officer's office were connected in the command of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had in my office a so-called battery of telephones. The chief of communications Milicija Petrovic had installed that. That was actually one phone with three indicators on top, or rather three buttons and three red lights. This telephone was connected to a PTT number and also a military number that could have been reached through the exchange. An identical telephone was with the Chief of Staff, with his own numbers, and another telephone was with the operations duty officer who was able to answer both from the office of the commander, and the office of the Chief of Staff. For example, if someone calls me, my telephone would ring, the operations duty officer sees the lamp flashing on the same set, and if after a certain period of time this lamp doesn't stop blinking, which means that I hadn't answered the phone, then the operations duty officer answers the call. The same happens if anybody wants to speak to the Chief of Staff while he is not in the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And would the incoming caller know that the call was being taken by someone other than the person he had asked the switchboard to put him through to?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The caller would know who he was calling and he would expect that person to answer. However, as I described, it might happen that somebody else answers the phone, not the person that he initially originally called, that the phone is answered by the duty operations officer instead.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now can we go to another document under seal. P1102. And before it is put on to the screen, I don't believe there are any initials on this document which would offend the public gallery seeing it. It's B in the B/C/S. A in the English. In the B/C/S it's the passage at the bottom of the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As has been rightly pointed out to me, the document is under seal and it cannot be broadcasted anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, yes. I thought we'd adopt the same practice as last time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, in the English it says "Obrenovic." What does it say in the B/C/S, Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Serbian it says "Obrenovicu," which indicates that the caller is addressing the person by the name of Obrenovic. That's a case, a grammatical case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And then there's obviously a period where something could not be heard or transcribed, and then the caller says: "Where is your commander? "As far as I know he is here. "He's not, he isn't answering. Listen, please tell him that I called, that Mane, Laco's deputy, will call him, that the police in Konjevic Polje have been told to do the same as the Engineering Battalion are doing, and that he can give orders to them through the commander of the Engineering Battalion. Okay. That's it. Take care." Is it possible to work out what's going on in this short conversation, Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is how I understand this conversation: The caller dialled Dragan Obrenovic's number, and when somebody else answered at the other end, he addressed this person by saying Obrenovicu. We don't have a record of what this person responded, but most probably this person was not the Obrenovic that he was looking for. And, therefore, the caller is asking where is your commander, and so on and so forth. Then they went on to discuss things and that is between the caller and the person who is not Obrenovic actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And who might have picked up a telephone call that was intended for the Chief of Staff, if he wasn't answering?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I described, it might have been the duty operations officer. And we seen a note in the log-book of the duty operations officer which is similar to something that we see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Who was in command of the Zvornik Brigade on the morning of the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Is there one word of truth in the suggestion that you were in the command of the Zvornik Brigade on the morning of the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there isn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Is there one word of truth in the suggestion that you spoke to Dragan Obrenovic on the morning of the 12th of July in the command of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there isn't either.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where were you at about 5 to 8.00 in the morning on the 12th of July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I was in Srebrenica, or rather, the village of Gostilj, inspecting the positions of my units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes, I let you proceed beyond the --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: That is absolutely the right moment to take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because I think it was not proper to stop you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: No, I thank you very much for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, did you go anywhere in the later morning of the morning of the 12th of July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the morning of the 12th of July, I when to the sector of the Bojna repeater where I was met by Colonel Vicic and General Krstic. I also believe that other brigade commanders were there as well. This is where we received full instructions for further operations for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The Bojna repeater, is that the same radio installation you were talking about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And was the meeting by arrangement?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had been called to report there, and I did that at the request of the Chief of Staff of the corps, which is General Krstic, so it must have been arranged.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Called that morning or previously?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just before the meeting itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right. Do you remember precisely who was there, or can you give us a rough estimate as to the number of people?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were Colonel Andric, Colonel Trivic, I was there, Colonel Vicic, General Krstic, I'm not sure about Colonel Blagojevic, whether he was there or not, I don't think he was. And I can't remember anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what tasks were you given at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to make a distinction between the term "meeting" and what took place at that time. What happened on that morning was not actually a meeting. This was just the issuing of task, and it can take place anywhere and at any time, so we were just standing there and received the tasks, and the task was for the units to head towards Srebrenica-Viogor-Suceska and to scour the ground along that axis and then gradually move on via Milici and Vlasenici towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What you just said was translated at scour the ground, what in practical terms were you told to do?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we still didn't know any details about the whereabouts of the 28th Division, we supposed that on the Srebrenica-Viogor-Suceska axis, it would be possible to trace elements of the 28th Division. And for that purpose, it was necessary to search the terrain and that area. My specific task was to move as a reserve along the road, whereas these two combat groups from the 2nd Romanija Brigade and the 1st Birac Brigade would search the ground on the left and right sides of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In which directions was it believed that the 28th Division might be heading?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point on the morning of the 12th, I only had an estimate about what route they -- the 28th Division might have taken, and I already said that. At that time, I didn't have any other fresh information.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Forgive me, Mr. Pandurevic, but it was a rather subtly different question. It wasn't your belief, it was what others might have believed as to the directions they were heading?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Krstic most probably believed that elements of the 28th Division might be found on the route that I mentioned. That's why he ordered us to proceed along that route, scour the ground there, and he also believed that most of the division had already been en route either towards Kladanj or Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And was this a task given just to you and your units or to everybody who was assembled at -- at the repeater, at Bojna?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those of us who received our tasks by Bojna were supposed to take the following route. Srebrenica-Viogor-Suceska, Derventa-Milici-Vlasenici, and then we were supposed to continue moving towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And how long did the meeting last and where did you go after it was over?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a very brief meeting. We had already had our general task that we received in the evening on the 11th. According to that task, we were supposed to move in the direction of Zepa. This was just providing us with the details in terms of the control of the ground en route of our march. In the afternoon hours we started leaving the area of Srebrenica. That was on the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And how did you leave?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units set out on foot. The units of the DG gradually assembled in the territory of Srebrenica. They formed a column and moved along the route. Before that I went to Zeleni Jadar where I found the logistics elements of the tactical group, I visited some wounded soldiers, and Major Dragutinovic, I took Major Dragutinovic with me and I joined the unit en route towards Viogor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was there any problem with Major Dragutinovic on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 11th of July during a NATO bombardment, he was the closest to the impact wave and he suffered some consequences. That's why he had to be evacuated and kept at the outpatient's clinic of the tactical group that was stationed in Zeleni Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And where did the unit move to during the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of the 12th of July, the unit reached the area of Viogor and Mount Jahorina. In an a orchard there immediately by the road, we organised a room in a tent. Night fell soon thereafter and that's where we spent that night.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were your units engaged in scouring the ground as it's being translated?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, my units were not engaged in that. We were kept in reserve and we were moving exclusively along the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Whose units were doing that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The units of the 2nd Romanija Brigade and the 1st Birac Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And why were they doing that rather than your units?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The operations commander, General Krstic, believed that in the previous combat operations DG was exposed to most pressure and was exhausted as a result of that. That's why he decided that the aforementioned forces should be put in front and that I, on the other hand, with my units, should be placed in reserve.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what time did you stop marching on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we reached Viogor, i.e., Mount Jahorina.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I don't know if something got lost there, but I asked you what time you stopped marching on the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was sometime after 1700 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you've told us about a meeting that occurred in the morning of the 12th of July, was that the only time you saw General Krstic that day?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, in the course of that afternoon on the 12th, once we arrived in the area of Viogor. As far as I can remember around 1800 hours, General Krstic also arrived there and that's when I saw him again and I actually met with him again there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did he have any particular purpose to come to see you, or was it just by chance you saw him?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he behaved as any other commander would have done under such circumstances. He wanted to see how far his units had reached, whether we had collected any information about the elements of the 28th Division that were lagging behind. He wanted to inspect our situation, and he wanted to see whether we were prepared to keep on moving the following day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you talk to him about the whereabouts of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I conveyed to him the information that we had received during our march. The information was to the effect that we had encountered some parts of the equipment, a cannon, B1, 76 millimetres, and some other parts of military equipment. However, we did not see any units. We did not see any troops. That's what I told him. And again I expressed my concern about the main body of the 28th Division. I asked him whether he had any precise or more precise information about the intentions of the 28th Division and about its whereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what did he say?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that the intentions and the whereabouts of the 28th Division were known, that the intelligence was received, that the division was moving in the direction of the Zvornik region en route to Tuzla, and that measures had already been put in place by other units of the Drina Corps, the Milic and the Bratunac Brigades, parts of the 65th Protection Motorised Regiment, and that the control of the ground and roads are as carried out by the special police units of the security centre in Zvornik. I was also told that my concern was without any foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you express any views?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say anything. I said if that was the case, then there's no reason for me to keep on worrying about that, if what General Krstic said was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you discuss the situation of the civilians you'd seen at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the fact that I had passed through Potocari on the 11th, and I'd seen that a large mass of civilians that were gathered in that area, and on the 11th in the evening at the meeting I was still seized with the thought that that situation had to be resolved in one way or another. I did ask about the situation and what was going on with all those people. Krstic told me that they had expressed a desire to be evacuated in the direction of Tuzla and Kladanj, and that the process was actually underway.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we just go back to something that you said earlier. The police units that were part of the operation that General Krstic described to you, where were they from and what were they.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Krstic did not mention the name of any MUP units. He just spoke in general terms and said that special police [as interpreted] units were also there and that they came from the security services centre in Zvornik. And this was a notorious fact. To be more precise, those units were under the command of the Colonel Vasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, please don't overlap. Can you repeat, Mr. Lazarevic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's just a matter of translation. Mr. Pandurevic was referring to PJP, and so far this was translated as PJP. And here we have in transcript special police. So this does make a difference in our submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, yes, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, we agree with that. That's the same issue you will recall a long while back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you agree with that as well, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I was just trying to help. A note had been passed to me, was just trying to clarify if for Borovcanin's lawyers and I failed. But it's been cleared up by others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So then we can proceed. Thank you both -- or the three of you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Forgive me, I've for gotten where we've got to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yeah. Were you given any further orders or tasks by General Krstic on the evening of the 12th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Krstic ordered me to spend the night there and that the following morning on the 13th, I continued marching en route Viogor-Suceska-Derventa-Milici-Vlasenici-Han Pijesak-Rijeka village. He also told me up there I would receive more concrete tasks for combat operations with regard Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I don't know if you still have your little car antenna, but if you could just point, please, to the march that you undertook on the day of the 12th from Srebrenica to Viogor? You are pointing now to Viogor, are you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you can see where it says TG1 and flag 1, this is the area where we spent the night on the 12th of July. And, therefrom, this is the route that we took. This is depicted by arrows across Suceska-Derventa-Milici, from Milici across Vlasenica to Han Pijesak and from Han Pijesak we arrived in the village of Rijeka. This is the area that I'm pointing to now marked again by a flag bearing number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now can we move to the morning of the 13th of July. What time did you move off on the morning of the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I can't give you the exact time. However, as soon as the units were ready, and as soon as the marching column was formed, we started marching.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you receive any visit on the morning of the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, on the 13th of July in the morning in the same place where General Krstic arrived on the 12th, General Krstic came again to the same place accompanied by General Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you expecting them?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not expect to see them again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What was the purpose of their visit?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to General Mladic, when he asked where -- about the whereabouts of units from the 1st Romanija -- 2nd Romanija and 1st Bircani Brigades, he wanted to talk to the soldiers, to motivate them, to prep them, and inspire them to proceed with combat activities. Later on I learned that Colonel Trivic had requested something of the sort from Mladic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What happened after General Krstic and General Mladic got there?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since my unit was gathered there, which means that we were not otherwise engaged, General Mladic addressed the soldiers briefly using staple military phrases, and he said that as of that day, it would be General Krstic who would take over the command over the corps and that he would be in command of the Drina Corps as from then onwards. He didn't stay long. Actually the two of them did not stay long. They left after a short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what about any further instruction, order, or task for you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nothing special. General Krstic only said, Keep on in line of the task, proceed towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, did you discuss on the morning of the 13th of July the whereabouts of the 28th Division?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I took the opportunity, and General Mladic's presence on Viogor. In Viogor he told me on the 11th, when I asked about the whereabouts of the 28th Division, and I asked him a similar thing. It was more of my obstinance. I did not really expect to hear anything new. He said, don't you worry, any such problems will be dealt with in an adequate way.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was there any discussion on that morning about the people that you'd seen at Potocari?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As far as I can remember, nothing was said about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was anything said about the capture of prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, again nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I want now to have a look at a document with you. This is 7D941.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, you gave us a fairly full description yesterday of what an Order to March is, and why it is created and what its purpose is, so I don't think we need to go into that again, but how did this document come to be created and when?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, as you can see in the heading, it says, "The Command of the Tactical Group of the Zvornik Brigade," dates back to the 13th of July. That's when it was created. And one can see in the order that it concerns the same echelons as the order for the 4th of July, which means that the tactical group showed an identical composition. I issued this order orally. I didn't know that operative Dragutinovic ever typed this order, I don't even think that I signed it. However, he is a very committed and responsible man and he put my order on paper. The first time I saw this order written up was here. I'm not sure that I saw it on the 13th of July when it was issued orally. I'm sure that I issued this Order to March orally.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Is it in Dragutinovic's handwriting?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is his handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And do you recall whether you gave the oral order on the 13th, and if so, at what point in the day?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I issued the oral order. I'm sure that I issued it immediately before the march started, but I can't be sure of the exact time that was. In any case, it was in the early morning hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Why was an order for march given on the 13th and not the day before on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because on the 12th we had another task and that was to scour the terrain, and our role was the role of reserve, and then we were supposed to proceed marching from the Viogor location towards Zepa because it is not the same tactical situation if you are a reserve on the one hand or if you are marching on the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. So what did you do, if it's not an obvious question, on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We started marching according to the deployment of the echelons as per the order. And during the march we encountered a lot of problems because the road was not very good and at one point we encountered anti-tank mines. And one APC got stuck so the whole column had to wait for that part of the road to be cleared.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: How long did you march on the 13th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In view of the number of kilometres that you can see in our route, our march was very long and this was partly due to the reasons that I've already mentioned. The second reason for a long march was the fact that we stopped in Vlasenici to refuel and then we continued moving towards the village of Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What time did you stop to refuel?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that we stopped during the night, or rather, around midnight.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have a look at P177.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, while this document is being enlarged so that everybody can read the detail of it, just tell us what it is?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document that we can see on the screen is the list of receipt and issuance of fuel and lubricants. This was issued by the technical organ of the logistics of the Drina Corps. We can see military post 71/11. This document could be found at petrol stations where vehicles were refueled. It bears a number under which it was issued and the date when it was issued, and then you can see that listed here are vehicles with the travel orders and the numbers there are the registration numbers and the quantities of the fuel issued to them. This list shows a list of the vehicles of the tactical group which were refueled at this particular petrol station.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, just a few questions so that we can, as it were, cross refer it to another document we are going to see in a minute. There is a number in the top left-hand corner which is 21/6-625. Do you know what the significance of that number is?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not a technical officer, but as a company commander in the JNA I had an opportunity to see these type of documents. This number indicates the number under which this document was registered in the book of issuance of fuel and lubricants. So there is a higher -- a document or a - so to speak - higher order that you can reference this document to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if we go, as it were, to the diagonal opposite, there's signature of a registered -- sorry, signature of an authorizing officer. Whose signature would that be, or should that be?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot read either the name or the signature in the original document. In English I see the name Vasiljevic. I don't know who that person is. I think that this should be the person working at this pump and who issued the fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, going back up to the top right-hand corner, we see in box number 4, the date of the 13th of July. What would or should that represent?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the date when this list was opened at the pump.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if we look at the numerous vehicles that appear to have been refueled, the date next to all of them is the 14th of July. Why was that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The refueling was taking place during the night so if it started around midnight, it might have gone on to the next day and that is probably the reason why we have the date the 14th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Is that your recollection, that the refueling took place in the small hours of the morning of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And forgive me, you might have already told us this, but where is this fuel pump, this gas station?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This petrol station is at the entrance to the town of Vlasenica when you arrive from Zvornik. This station was used by the logistics department of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can we just go down to entry 13, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The name on the far right-hand side is Dragan Stevic. You've already told us the name of your driver. Is that his name?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the name and the signature of my driver who was given 68 -- or, rather, correction, 48 litres of fuel on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the number plate T-2175, is that the registration number of the car we saw on the video yesterday, the Nissan Patrol?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably it is. We can check it on the travel order because that would also contain the licence plate number.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'll try to keep up with you, Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We'll go to that now then, shall we. 7D91, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: By and large I prefer these documents in the Serbian, the translation doesn't really add very much. But this is the -- what's called the vehicle work log relating to a Nissan T-2175 for the period the 1st to the 31st of July, and the drivers of that vehicle were Dragan Stevic and Bogdan Pandurevic. Just out of interest, any relative?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is my cousin. He stood in for Dragan Stevic as a driver when the former was absent.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And if we go down to the 14th of July of 1995. We see document number 21/6-625. The same number we saw on the previous fuel log, 48 litres of fuel, and a signature. And just while we are here, whose signature should appear under the column "manager's signature"?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you said, this travel work log shows the document on the basis of which the vehicle was fueled and that was the document 01/6-625, and the handler's signature was the signatures of the person actually working at the pump and filling the tanks of the vehicles. And this is to certify that this person actually issued the fuel to whom he was supposed to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thanks. Who was travelling with you at that stage on the night of the 13th and 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean with me in the vehicle, or?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Good question. Yes, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course my driver, Dragan Stevic. Two escorts, soldiers, and a signalsman. Whether Mijo Dragutinovic was with me in the car or whether he was in another car, I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And where did you go after you had refueled?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After all the vehicles had been refueled, I formed a marching column, checked the situation, and we headed towards Han Pijesak and then the village of Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Anything memorable about that night that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that in the early morning hours, perhaps around 2.00 of the 14th of July, we arrived in the village of Rijeka, that we set up a make-shift camp, put up a tent, and that I slept for a few hours. The other units were also deployed in the same area and we were waiting for the dawn.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we go to the second page, please, of the document on our screen currently, 7D91.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I'd like to focus, please, with you, Mr. Pandurevic, on the entries for the 11th, 12th, 13th, and 14th of July. I don't think we need to look at the number of persons apparently carried. That is always constant. It's really the entries. The 11th of July, Zeleni Jadar local. The 12th of July, Zeleni Jadar-Srebrenica. The 13th of July Srebrenica-Bratunac. 14th of July, Srebrenica-Han Pijesak. Can you explain the entries for the 11th to the 14th of July to us, please?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When a motor vehicle is used, each driver obliged to register the route that the vehicle would take or had taken. The normal practice is to fill in this box before the vehicle sets off. This is an evident example how during combat it was very difficult for a driver to fill in the routes of movement, because these routes were unpredictable, sudden, sometimes shorter, sometimes longer. They are not related to any residential areas or any known features, and particularly the driver is not familiar with the names of these features. And we see here that the driver Stevic sometimes registered actual routes and sometimes he just filled it in in order to justify the mileage he made in the course of a day, because at the end of each month the fuel consumption is calculated and it has to tally with the mileage.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do the journeys apparently recorded for those days reflect in any any way the journeys he and you were taking?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my recollection to a very low extent. Very little. For example, on the 11th, I wasn't in Zeleni Jadar at all. Maybe the driver went there for some reason, but I didn't. So it is very difficult for me to understand why we see these routes recorded as they are.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: On the 13th of July did you travel from Srebrenica to Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't, because on the 13th we left Viogor and took the route that I already told you about.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And before we come to the detail of it, on the 14th of July, did you travel from Srebrenica to Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As you can see, we travelled -- as you can see from the previous documents and the order, we travelled on the Viogor-Milici-Han Pijesak route. But, obviously, Srebrenica was a destination that served to him as a kind of bench-mark for all the movements.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I want to show you now, please, P114.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is what we've come to call Stupcanica 95. The combat order for Stupcanica 95. When did you first see this?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I first saw this order and received it on the 14th of July at the forward command post at Kravice, that is the former command post of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: When did you arrive at Kravice?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the morning of the 14th after the dawn when we woke up, it might have been around 10.00. I went to the Kravice forward command post, reported to General Krstic, and received my order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where all your units then present?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I went to the forward command post to receive the order, the units remained in the so-called expecting region in the village of Rijeka. They were waiting for me to give them specific tasks for further movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And can we go to page 2 of the document now then, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We see your written task at point 4 there, the Zvornik Infantry Brigade from Podzeplje-Brloznik area shall attack the enemy along the village of Pertici, village of Cavcici, Zepa axis in order to crush the enemy along the line of attack. Reach the Palez-Borak line and continue the advance. The next task is to reach Zepa. Just give us some sort of picture of this. When your corps commander, as he by then was, gives you an order like this, does he sit you down, point the paragraph out to you and tell what you it means, or does he just hand you a piece of paper or does he tell you what you've got to do?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I wasn't alone at the forward command post when I received this order. I think then some other brigade commanders were there as well. We were given the order, we read it, and the corps commander gave us some additional instructions as regards the execution of the tasks that we had been given. I informed him that I understood the task, and I went back to my unit. And then I started taking the unit from the expecting region to the deployment area in anticipation of an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'd just like you please, to point out to us where Krivaca is on the map behind you, which will then enable us to get rid of it so that the public gallery can see the Court more clearly.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you see this rectangular flag, this is where the Drina Corps forward command post was. This is Krivaca under the Velika Zepa mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Actually, it's a nice break when this could be done. I'd just like to introduce now two exhibits to show the movements of tactical group 1 and the movements of General Pandurevic as set out in the evidence he's already given. And the first of those is 7D1059. And this, again, is an attachment to the report of Admiral Antic. And we might as well just play them both so that we can see, as it were, the differences between the two videos. Well, I'm not going to lose any time. If this is going to take a little while to come on, there are a few questions I can fill the time with.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What did you understand the task or the objective of Stupcanica 1995 to be?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the order itself relating to Stupcanica 95, clear tasks have been assigned to the units and the targets of attack, and these were primarily forces of the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters would kindly ask the witness to repeat the name of the unit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
