utterances.text: Sorry to stop you like this, but the interpreters need you to repeat the name of the units, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I didn't say the name of the units. I said the units of the Army of Republika Srpska. And the target of attack were the forces of the Zepa Brigade whereas the civilian population and UNPROFOR were not the targets of the actions of the VRS. And I would also like to add that this order and Stupcanica 95 operation, unlike Krivaja 95, included some other units that were not involved in combat operations in Krivaja 95 operation. And these units had already been partly involved in combat activities around Zepa. And for that reason, General Mladic was rushing the forces on the 11th from Krivaja 95 operation to head as soon as possible to Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you understand the objective of the operation to be to take the town itself?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zepa is a large village with a number of hamlets around it. It is very inaccessible because it is in the mountainous area. And this task, as far as I can remember, as it was formulated, the units were supposed to reach the area of Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And then do what?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To neutralise the Zepa Brigade, and this neutralisation would be effected either by disarming it and making it to surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: There's an "either" in the sentence you just said. Did you offer an alternative to my question other than disarming it and making it surrender?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the military vocabulary, when one carries out tasks, you can use terms such as "neutralise enemy forces" or destroy -- and "destroy enemy forces." The destruction of enemy forces is self-explanatory. That means to inflict as many losses on them so that they would no longer pose a combat or military threat. To neutralise means -- doesn't mean to destroy, but it means to bring them to -- into such a situation that they are no longer able to put up resistance by either making threat, or by voluntary agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This is what we heard the witness say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, in military terms on the 14th of July after you had received the order from General Krstic, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After we received the order, I led my unit from the Rijeka village sector to the sector of Podzeplje near a school. I deployed them into a combat line and from the Podzeplje sector we launched an attack along the Podzeplje-Brloznik village and Brloska mountain axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What were the respective positions of your line and the defence lines of the Zepa Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Podzeplje area, the VRS units had been deployed from before. I think it was a battalion made up of members of an older age, and it was part of the 65th Motorised Regiment. And for a number of years they had been in these same positions. At about 1 and a half to 2 kilometres from their positions were the positions of the Zepa Brigade. And I engaged my units in the combat through the positions of this battalion and covered this no-man's land which was about 2 kilometres wide. That all happened on the 14th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And how far was that from the village of Zepa itself?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly speaking about 10 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And was there much fighting on the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were sporadic skirmishes and fighting where the forces of the Zepa Brigade opened machine-gun fire from the surrounding peaks, and we responded by firing back. There was no shifting of the frontline of the Zepa Brigade during that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And where did you spend the night of the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spent the night in the school there. In Podzeplje, the school did not have either a door or any windows. It was in a bad state of repair. Most of the command spent the night with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, we're going to have another go at playing these two short sections of video. And would you watch them, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just so it's in the record, those two videos have two separate surrogate sheets. The first is 7D1058, the second is 7D1059. And everybody has been disclosed that along with the other appendices to Admiral Antic's expert report, but if there's anything else we can do to assist anybody accessing that material, we will of course do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you've already given, I think, all the, as it were, stop off points of your journey between the 4th and the 14th of July, but did the first of those videotapes accurately reflect the movement of your units in that period?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I believe that it does completely. The only thing is that perhaps for technical reasons at arrow was moved too much to the west from Srebrenica before it forked off towards Viogor.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you for that. And the second of those videos, did that accurately reflect, perhaps with that one same caveat, your own personal movements in the periods of the 4th to the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, by this point, namely the 14th of July, had you made contact with the command of the Zvornik Brigade since the time you left Zvornik on the 4th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as my memory serves me, on the 5th of July I used RU-1 radio relay equipment at the IKM of the Drina Corps at Pribicevac, and I established communication with the Zvornik Brigade. Because I had realised that the tank company was missing grenades and I asked for the grenades to be supplied. And I remember another case, on the 7th of July, I believe, on the day when there was no combat due to adverse weather conditions, I remembered some teaching materials that should have been photocopied and delivered to the students of the school of technology. The thought just occurred to me on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we have placed into e-court, please, now, and I think we are going to give you the hard copy from now on because it's a document we'll be referring to repeatedly. But can we have P377, the duty officer's notebook of the Zvornik Brigade, page 96 in both documents. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you will need to know the ERN number, Mr. Pandurevic, it's 5714 are the last four letters.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've got it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: About half to two-thirds of the way -- well, halfway down the page, do you see the name Cvetko Pavlovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And just below that an entry which says "50 tank rounds of 100 millilitres."

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says 50 tank grenades or rounds.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, that's all a bit enigmatic, but can you confirm for us that that is an entry on the 5th of July, can you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see the date 6 of July on the following page. However, on the previous page -- yes, the 5th of July which points to the conclusion that this note does refer to the 5th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, let's see if we can get a better record of events. P378, the war diary at B/C/S -- sorry, the duty operations officer's diary. B/C/S page 83. The English translation is 7D1075. Yes, please, Ms. Stewart, that's very helpful. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Pandurevic, you're looking for the last four numbers, 6685. And have you got that page, Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unbelievable, it opened precisely on that page. And I would like to thank Mr. McCloskey for allowing me to have this document in my hands for the first time ever in my whole life.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can you read the entry at 1700 hours, please?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says Commander Pandurevic called and asked for 50 rounds of 100 millimetre. Ljubo Bojanovic informed the assistant commander for logistics."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We can see that that's the 5th of July by looking further at the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, we'll just go through that exercise quickly in relation to the 7th of July, before we take the break, if that's okay with everybody. Can we look now at P377 again. B/C/S and English page 101. And if Mr. Pandurevic can be handed back the original of the duty operations officer's log-book. He is looking for 5719 is the last four numbers on the ERN.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I've got that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you should find an entry at 1110 in the morning, which reads: "Brigade commander reported from Zeleni Jadar region" -- I'm sorry, I'm reading the wrong one. "Colonel Pandurevic called. They are well. They worked, materials to be taken and handed to the faculty." And you've already told us what that referred to. What did you teach, just out of interest?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that I found this note in the log-book identical as you presented it. At that time I was the assistant in sociology since this was a school of technology and social ecology was one of the subjects within sociology, and this happened to have been my masters thesis. I was selected as the best suited person to teach that particular subject at that school.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Said with your usual modesty, Mr. Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we turn to P378 and you are looking at 6686, and we need B/C/S page 84. And the English translation is for the 7th of July.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that in the original as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can you read us, please, the entry for 1110?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "The brigade commander reported from the Zeleni Jadar sector. The situation in the unit is good," as signed by the duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, just to conclude the topic, other than those two calls made from the forward command post, as you've told us, did you contact the command of the Zvornik Brigade at all between the 4th and the 14th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'd done it during that period, it would have been reflected in one of the two documents that we have just seen here. To the best of my recollection, I did not have any such contacts.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And that would be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll have a 25-minute break starting now, it's quarter past noon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: During the period the 4th to the 14th of July, did anybody from the Zvornik Brigade get in contact with you? I should specify, from the command of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody from the command of the Zvornik Brigade attempted to contact me. Nobody from Zvornik did either.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: To be honest this might be obvious, but was your advice or view sought on any decision taken by brigade command during that period?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And just to clear this up, on the 11th of July, you have told us that you were in the command of the Bratunac Brigade. Did you take the opportunity then to make contact with the brigade command in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not make any contacts with them. I was still performing my tasks and I was under the immediate command of General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: While we are recapping on the period of your absence, I just want to go through with you a few things that were going on at the Zvornik Brigade during that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And can we start, please, by having in e-court P110.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, this is the Drina Corps order of the 12th of July for the provision of buses for the evacuation from the Srebrenica enclave. And it was sent, amongst other people, to the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade. On the 12th of July, did you know anything about that order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know anything about this order. This order went straight to the command of the Zvornik Brigade, and it was Mr. Obrenovic who acted upon this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did he need your authority to accept the order and comply with it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all. He was directly subordinated to the corps command, he received his orders from him and he was duty-bound to act upon those orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you consulted as to whether that order should be complied with?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody consulted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, can we have a look please, at P157.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And this is another Drina Corps order of the 12th of July of 1995, addressed not to so many brigades this time but to the 1st Zvornik Infantry Brigade, and it concerns an order to regulate traffic on the Konjevic Polje-Bratunac road, and it says: "The command of the 1st Zvornik Brigade will assign a motorised patrol of the military traffic police to regulate the traffic at the Konjevic Polje junction. The priority shall be given to buses travelling from Srebrenica. Take over the Konjevic Polje junction at 1630 on the 12th of July." I mean, firstly, was that order delivered to you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was sent straight to the command of the Zvornik Brigade. It was never delivered to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did Dragan Obrenovic need your authority to accept or comply with that order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he made decisions in compliance with this order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did anybody contact you to see whether you thought it was a good idea for that order to be complied with?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody did. If this would have happened, the thing that you are asking me about, then the function of the deputy commander or the person standing in for commander in his absence would be deprived of any sense. And this function could be performed by anybody who can dial a telephone number, establish contact, and ask the commander - who wasn't there - what to do. However, a deputy or a person standing in for the commander is considered to be qualified to make independent decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, let's follow these things through a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: P322, please. The regular combat report for the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Again, can we see from paragraph 2 of that order that the brigade on that day sent to Bratunac, pursuant to your order, eight buses from Drina trans, two buses from our military post, and four of our trucks; and one military police detachment was sent to Konjevic Polje pursuant to your order. What can we deduce from that document?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can deduce were this combat is that in the regular combat report the command of the Zvornik Brigade, i.e., Dragan Obrenovic, reports to the command of the Drina Corps that in everything they acted upon the order that I received from them, and the order concerned all the things listed in here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Just to deal with one feature of this document. Can we go quickly to page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It bears your typed signature. Were you in the command of the Zvornik Brigade on the 12th of July at ten past 5.00 in the afternoon?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. You can see that this regular combat report does not bear my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you know of or approve the contents of that report before it was sent to Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we just look at a page from the duty officer's notebook for the same day, the 12th of July, to give ourselves some further examples. So it's P377 in e-court. English pages 114. Sorry, the pages are the same, page 114 in both documents. And if -- thank you, Ms. Stewart.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If Mr. Pandurevic could look at page 5732 in the hard copy. While we're getting there, you've dealt with this on a number of occasions before, but why would your block signature appear on a report when you were out of the brigade's command and commanding another unit?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that we have already discussed that. I believe that it was either on the first day or the second day of my testimony. There were different variations when it comes to block signature. Sometime it is would be my name, sometimes the Chief of Staff's name, or a third person's name. It all depended on who the operations duty officer was and how that person understood the situation. And according to that understanding, he would use one of the names in the block signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm interested in looking at in the English, so you can find it yourself in the original document, a large section that appears from -- that begins with the phrase "The 1st Platoon of the military police ambush at Dzafin Kamen. The 1st platoon of the 4th infantry battalion, Tisova Kosa ambush." And then a reference to the Drina Corps order. And then further down: "Radika requested assistance in manpower to stop the Turks. We are sending a Praga." A section we've looked at before. What are these records of in the duty officer's notebook?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These records in this notebook reflect the events during that period in the territory in Zvornik, i.e., in the Zvornik Brigade. The duty operations officer pursuant to Dragan Obrenovic's interventions or interventions by some other persons enters all the activities that were underway or records orders that were to be conveyed to some units.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And the 1st platoon of the military police ambush at Dzafin Kamen. What does that appear to reflect?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that the 1st platoon of the military police company was tasked with going to Dzafin Kamen, which was south-west of Zvornik. They were supposed to set up an ambush there. I suppose elements of the 28th Division were expected to appear on that axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Anybody ask you whether they should do that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These were independent decisions taken by Dragan Obrenovic who was standing in for the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And going to the bottom of the page, anybody ask you whether a Praga should be sent to Radika?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did it appear from the document you just saw, the combat report of the 12th of July, that that was done?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, you'll be able to do this a lot quicker than the rest of us, but can you turn to page 5733 in the duty officer's notebook, which is the next page. In the e-court copy that's page 115. Now, there's a very long section that begins: "After the take-over of the Srebrenica...," can you see it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm not going to read it out because I'll do it too quickly and infuriate the interpreters, but we can all read it to ourselves. What does that record?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order. In its first part, basic information about the enemy are given. In this particular instance these are the units of the 28th Division. Based on his own assessment and information Obrenovic provided these details, and based thereon to all commanders except of the 6th infantry battalion he issued tasks and ordered measures to be taken. This telegram was recorded by the duty operations officer and forwarded to the battalion command in this form.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Again, at the risk of being repetitive, did you have any input on the decision-making process and the making of that order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we go over one more page to 5734. And page 116 in the e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I might have allowed things to slip a little, Mr. Pandurevic, what date are we on now on page 5734?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The previous date was the 12th of July and I'm following the pages. The handwriting is the same. I think that what we have just discussed on page 5734 also bears the date of the 12th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Now, I'm interested in the entry in the middle of that page: "The 4th and 7th Battalions, everything all right. Measures taken pursuant to order, the 2nd Battalion, the 7th and 4th Battalion, conscripts are to..." something "... lines to the maximum - at least three of them should stand guard." And what does that entry record?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word that you couldn't read says that they should become completely serious. This is another order issued directly to the battalions on the frontline to be fully in combat readiness for possible combat engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you consulted about or did you know about the making of that order by Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anything about it and nobody consulted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we look at P1032, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is the Drina Corps order of the 13th of July to prevent the passage of Muslim groups to Tuzla and Kladanj. And after a preamble, it reads in the English: "I hereby order brigade commands in their areas of responsibility will employ all available able-bodied men to discover, block, arm, capture any Muslim groups observed and prevent their crossing into Muslim territory. Set rounds the clock ambushes along the entire Zvornik-Crni Vrh-Sekovici-Vlasenica, arrange protection for people and property in Serbian villages along the route taken by the groups. And, to this end, engage all who can carry a gun. Vigorously prevent individual departures from villages. Put captured and disarmed Muslims in suitable buildings that can be secured by small forces and immediately inform the superior command." Did General Krstic or General Zivanovic deliver that order to you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You were in contact with General Krstic on the 13th of July, did he tell you about that order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't tell me anything. I don't know at what time this order was sent out. I can't see it on the document. But in its preamble one can see that they have plenty information about the intentions of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And can we now go to P325.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is the Zvornik Brigade daily combat report of the 13th of July. And it records that the primary task for the units is: "In order to cut off groups of Turks retreating from Srebrenica towards Tuzla and to protect our brigade units we have taken the following steps." And then a whole list of steps are taken. How does this report to the corps command correspond to the document on the corps' order that we were just looking at?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This regular combat report issued by the Zvornik Brigade command contains what measures it had taken pursuant to the order and based on their own assessment. Some of these measures were recorded in the work log-book of the duty operations officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And so just to conclude this section, what do these various examples of the operation of the brigade tell us about who gave orders to Dragan Obrenovic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This clearly indicates that Dragan Obrenovic received his orders from the corps command and that he was under directly -- he was directly under their command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And his authority to comply with those orders?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows that pursuant to the principle of single authority -- singleness of command, he made decisions based on the decisions and orders from the command and based on his own assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Pandurevic, in the light of the way the Prosecution's case has been put, I'd like to ask you a series of specific questions about the actions of Dragan Obrenovic, and I need to put briefly into e-court a document which is under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that is P2911. So it should not be broadcast. And we need to look at page 2, paragraph 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, this is just as a preliminary. I assume you are aware that Dragan Obrenovic pleaded guilty to count 5 of his own indictment, a charge of persecutions. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew that he pleaded guilty, but to which counts from the indictment specifically, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Very well. Well, just to ground some future question, we are looking at paragraph 5 which reads in the English: "Dragan Obrenovic understands that he is pleading guilty to count 5 of the indictment" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please slow down when reading. MR. HAYNES.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: "... persecutions, a crime against humanity, specifically acknowledging and admitting his conduct as set forth in paragraphs 4-8, 15-27, 29-33, 36, 45, 46, 46.6-46.12," and some other paragraphs. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I realise what I've done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If we could go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: We can take that document off the screen because that is all I want to refer to, and we can put on to the screen in e-court, please, P2930, the indictment which is not, I think, anything other than a public document. And can we start, please, with paragraph 29 which is page 7 in the English and page 8 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. Now, everybody can see this, but I'll read it. This is paragraph 29, which as we know, he specifically acknowledged in his plea agreement and it says: "Dragan Obrenovic, during the time periods when he was the deputy commander, acting commander, or commander, is criminally responsible for the acts of his subordinates pursuant to Article 7(3) of the statute of the Tribunal if he knew or had reason to know that his subordinates were about to commit criminal acts or had done so and he failed to take the necessary and reasonable measures to prevent such acts or to punish the perpetrators thereof."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we now go please to paragraph 46.6 at page 15 in the English, page 16 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, this is another paragraph, the facts of which he specifically admitted pursuant to his plea agreement, and it relates to the crimes committed at Orahovac. And it reads: "In the late evening hours of 13th of July and during the day of the 14th of July 1995, personnel from the military police company of the Bratunac Brigade working together with other individuals and units transported hundreds of Bosnian-Muslim males from in and around Bratunac to the Grbavci school in the village of Orahovac. These Bosnian Muslim men had been captured from the column of men retreating from the the Srebrenica enclave or separated in Potocari. "On the 14th of July, 1995, VRS personnel, including members of the military police company of the Zvornik Brigade, under the command and control of Dragan Obrenovic, guarded and blindfolded the Bosnian Muslim males detained at the Grbavci school. In the early afternoon of the 14th of July, VRS personnel transported these Bosnian Muslim males from the school at Grbavci to a nearby field where personnel, including members of the 4th battalion of the Zvornik Brigade, under the command and control of Dragan Obrenovic, ordered the prisoners off the trucks and summarily executed them with automatic weapons. Approximately 1.000 Bosnian Muslim males were killed. "On the 14th and 15th of July, 1995, members of the Zvornik Brigade Engineering Company under the direction of Dragan Jokic used heavy equipment to bury the victims in mass graves at the execution site, while the executions continued. On the evening of the 14th of July, lights from the engineering machinery illuminated the execution and burial sites during the executions." Mr. Pandurevic, did you issue any order for any unit of the Zvornik Brigade to take part in any operation together with military policeman from Bratunac and/or other units to transport prisoners to the Grbavci school in the village of Orahovac.

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you aware that Dragan Obrenovic had given such order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that, and I believe it was not his place to give such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you consulted by Dragan Obrenovic or anybody else about the carrying out of such an operation?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't. I didn't know that that operation was in progress.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you give any order that military policemen from the Zvornik Brigade should be used to guard and blindfold prisoners at the Grbavci school?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you know that Dragan Obrenovic had given any such order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you consulted about whether any such thing should be done by Dragan Obrenovic or anybody else?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody consulted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you give any order that prisoners should be taken from the Grbavci school to a nearby school and executed?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you give any order that any unit of the Zvornik Brigade should take part in any such activity?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you give any order that any member of the Zvornik Brigade should take part in such an activity?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did Dragan Obrenovic consult you about whether he should give orders for the killing of prisoners to take place?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Had he asked you whether he should give such an order, what would you have said?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think this is what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's probably my fault for using the word "had" instead of "if."

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If he had consulted you about whether he should give an order to have prisoners killed, what would you have said?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would never have given him such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, this is really important, I'm going to try that again. If he had asked you about whether he should give such an order, what would you have said?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have told him not to issue such an order at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You've told us how you interpret paragraph 116 of the brigade rules, but is the killing of prisoners in the spirit of your command of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. I wasn't in command of the Zvornik Brigade at the time and there was not a single decision of mine that anyone could have referred to, including Dragan Obrenovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we go down the page now, please to paragraph 46. --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is that really responsive to your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I don't think it is, but I'll try again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Is killing prisoners part of the spirit of your command of the Zvornik Brigade?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Paragraph 46.7. The Petkovci school.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: "On the 14th of July 1995, VRS and/or MUP personnel transported approximately 1.000 Bosnian Muslim males from detention sites in and around Bratunac to the school at Petkovci. These Bosnian Muslim men had been captured from the column of men retreating from the Srebrenica enclave or separated in Potocari. On the 14th of July and the early morning hours of the 15th of July, VRS and/or MUP personnel struck, beat, and assaulted and shot with automatic weapons Bosnian Muslim males being detained at the school. "Dragan Obrenovic, as deputy commander commanding the Zvornik Brigade in the absence of the commander, exercised command, control, and coordination duties associated with the detention of prisoners at the Petkovci school." Did you issue any order for any unit of the Zvornik Brigade to take part in any operation alone or together with MUP units to transport prisoners to the Petkovci school?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you aware that Dragan Obrenovic had given any such order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you consulted by Dragan Obrenovic or anybody else about the carrying out of such an operation?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you give any order that any unit from the Zvornik Brigade should be used to beat, assault, or kill prisoners at the Pilica school?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you know that Dragan Obrenovic had given any such order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you consulted about whether any such thing should be done by Dragan Obrenovic or anybody else?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody consulted me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Had -- sorry, I'm about to make the same mistake again. If Dragan Obrenovic had asked you whether he should give such an order, what would you have said?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have told him not to issue such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we go to paragraph 46.8, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The dam near Petkovci: "On or about the evening of the 14th of July 1995 and the early morning hours of the 15th of July 1995, VRS personnel from the Zvornik Brigade, under the command and control of Dragan Obrenovic, including drivers and trucks from the 6th Infantry Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade, transported the surviving members of the group of approximately 1.000 Bosnian Muslim males from the school at Petkovci to an area below the dam near Petkovci. They were assembled below the dam and summarily executed by VRS or MUP soldiers with automatic weapons. "In the morning of the 15th of July, 1995, VRS personnel from the Engineering Company of the Zvornik Brigade, working under the direction of Dragan Jokic and together with other individuals and units, used excavators and other heavy equipment to bury the victims while the executions continued." Mr. Pandurevic, did you issue any order to the 6th Infantry Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade or any other unit to transport the prisoners to Petkovci dam?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you aware that Dragan Obrenovic had given any such order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you consulted by Dragan Obrenovic or anybody else about the carrying out of such an operation?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, either [as interpreted] Dragan Obrenovic or anybody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you give any order that the 6th Infantry Battalion of the Zvornik Brigade or any other unit to assemble and summarily execute the prisoners?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you know that Dragan Obrenovic had given any such order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you consulted by Dragan Obrenovic as to whether he should give such an order?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he didn't consult me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If he had consulted you, what would you have told him?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have told him not to do any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, we've got ten minutes so we'll move on from there. What happened on the morning of the 15th of July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of July, 1995, in the morning I was in the vicinity of Podzeplje. I ordered the units of the tactical group to proceed with combat activities in the spirit of the previously issued task in keeping with the Stupcanica 95 operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did there come a point where you were called away to go to the forward command post?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Who called you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The call came from the IKM of the Drina Corps. I believe it was Milenko Jevdjevic who called me, he was the signalsmen that, he conveyed a message to me to report to General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And did you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I went to the forward command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, we might just want to get the names of the individuals correct on the record. I don't think we did right, who called him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Would you -- you mentioned - I don't think there's any mystery about this - you mentioned the name of signalsman who called you to go to the forward command post and it didn't appear, so can you repeat it?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milenko Jevdjevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Who was at the forward command post when you got there?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I arrived there, I saw General Krstic, Major Jevdjevic, and some other soldiers, signalsmen, and some people from the office of the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you have a conversation with General Krstic?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not clear why he had called me. I reported to him. I asked him what the problem was. And as far as I can remember, he showed me some telegrams, some documents, which I read. He told me that he had certain problems on the combat lines of the Zvornik Brigade, and that Dragan Obrenovic had asked for reinforcement.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I just want to review some documents with you very quickly before the weekend.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can we have a look at P327, please, in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: This is the Zvornik Brigade interim combat report of the 14th of July which reads: "Tonight at around 2020 a large group of Muslims passed through the broader Maricici area proceeding towards the Zvornik-Caparde road. A column about 2 or 3 kilometres long and another part of a column were observed in the area of Josanica and Liplje." Do you recall whether that was one of the documents that General Krstic showed you on the morning of the 15th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the contents of a similar document, but I don't think that it was in the same shape or form. I believe it was in the shape of of a telegram which was subsequently typed on a teletypewriter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Very well. Can we move on to P169, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Could you tell us what the source of this document is and what sort of document it is?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document originates from the command of the Drina Corps. It represents a sort of notification or information. The information was obtained from the security centre in Zvornik. And this report also contains information on what the MUP units and the Zvornik Brigade units were up to. This telegram was signed by Colonel Jocic, Pedrag. He was in the operations organ of the Drina Corps, and this was delivered to the attention of General Krstic at the forward command post at Krivace.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And can you now recall whether this was one of the documents that General Krstic showed you on 15th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there were other documents bearing Colonel Jocic's signature. But this is more or less the kind of information that I was made aware of on that morning and I believe that I remember this.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Sorry to try your patience, Mr. Pandurevic, but just one more.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: P163, please. That's P163, just three digits. 163.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again read it through to yourself, I'm not going to read it out aloud to you. Can you recall whether this was a document you saw on that morning?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember a document issued by the radio surveillance platoon of the Drina Corps, they were engaged in listening in the radio relay communication of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I remember the contents as they are here; Naser Oric's name was mentioned, and the intentions of the BiH Army to link up the units of the 2nd Corps with elements of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Can you now recall how many documents in total General Krstic showed to you on that morning?

utterances.speaker: VINKO PANDUREVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember the contents of three documents similar to the ones that have been shown here. I don't know whether there were any other documents. I can't be sure of that and there's nothing I can say to that effect. At that moment, I was more interested in the contents or the information contained in the documents than in their numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Pandurevic, with the Mr. President's leave I think we'll leave it there for the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. Haynes. Mr. Haynes, where do we stand. You had estimated 30 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: If only.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 30 hours. 30 hours. So far we have consumed 13 hours or so. Where do we stand?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I think the estimate is going to be pretty much bang on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, okay. All right. That helps us plan pretty well, then. Thank you. We will reconvene on Monday morning at 9.00, and I wish everyone a happy weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 2nd day of February 2009 at 9.00 a.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
